papers/paper-24.pdf.subtitle: The Three-Register Dialectic of the Relational Real (《亲密关系中的文化涌现》)
papers/paper-24.pdf.teaser: Between two people a whole world gets spoken in words no third person can translate — private jokes, rituals, a shared grammar of meaning. This paper argues that this is culture in its most exposed form: not a finished thing that is handed down, but a generation that never closes, and it asks how such a culture is made, how capital reaches in to capture it, and what its just generation requires.
papers/paper-24.pdf.background: Culture is usually theorised as something finished and transmissible — a heritage handed down, a system of shared representations, a structure reproduced. This paper, Paper XXIV, takes up the first 'directed fissure' left open by Paper XXIII and argues that this picture misconceives what culture is. Culture is rightly conceived as a generation that does not close: the dialectical exteriorization, across the three registers of experience and under material constraint, of the interwoven generative history of relational subjects. And its minimal, most exposed unit is the intimate dyad — the two people between whom a whole world of meaning is spoken in words no third person can translate. Studying culture there, where it is smallest and most fragile, makes visible what larger-scale accounts of culture leave hidden.
papers/paper-24.pdf.approach: The paper is built in three parts — an ontology, a phenomenology, and an ethics. Part One works at the level of culture in general, passing through the major theories of cultural formation (transmission and collective representation; symbol and interpretation; structure and reproduction, including Bourdieu; culture as the encoding of power; the Chinese wen–hua tradition; and the dialogic) and locating within them a position they leave open. It states that position as a variant of the Lacanian theory of the three registers — the three-register dialectic of the relational Real — granting the Real a neglected relational form, showing culture to span all three registers, and setting the registers into a materially driven dialectical motion. Part Two turns to the intimate dyad, isolating five mechanisms that belong to it alone and reading the phenomena of private culture through them, with the family ethos (jiafeng) as a middle-scale case. Part Three gives the political economy and ethics: the production of intimate culture under material conditions, its capture by capital, and the condition of its just generation. Throughout, the method is dialectical and treats no theory as final; the paper carries an explicit AI-usage statement affirming the author's responsibility for every claim.
questions: Is culture a finished object that is transmitted, or a generation that never closes?
What do the major theories of culture (transmission, symbol, reproduction, power, wen–hua, the dialogic) leave open?
What would it mean to grant the Lacanian Real a relational form?
Why is the intimate dyad the minimal and most exposed unit of cultural emergence?
Which mechanisms of cultural formation belong to the dyad alone?
How does capital capture a culture it cannot simply seize — and what is lost when it does?
On what does the just generation of culture depend?

key_concepts.term: The three-register dialectic of the relational Real
key_concepts.gloss: The central thesis: culture is the dialectical exteriorization, across the three Lacanian registers (Imaginary, Symbolic, Real) and under material constraint, of the interwoven generative history of relational subjects — with the Real given a hitherto neglected relational form.

key_concepts.term: Culture as a generation that does not close
key_concepts.gloss: Culture is not a finished, transmissible object but an unfinished generation: it has no final truth, is never static, and develops through the historical sublation of its own forms.

Belonging to the intimate dyad alone: the vacant big Other (no external authority fixes meaning, so the two are each other's authority); the double interweaving of two structures of desire; high-density sedimentation at visible speed; the heightened configuration of the three registers; and fragility/reversibility.
A middle-scale case between the dyad and the wider culture, used to draw out the epistemology of a dialectical view of culture and the study of power within it.
Capital captures a relational culture not by seizing it but by preserving its symbolic form while drawing off its coherence in the Real — one of the paper's five theses.

A cultural form persists through changed conditions only insofar as it endogenously generates a counter-power against its own power — so just cultural generation must, in the same movement, generate the restraint of power.

Resistance to transfer rises with depth of anchoring in interwoven drive (non-transferability); externalizing symbolic authority trades endogeneity against stability (vacancy); resistance to power, capital, and time comes from anchoring in the Real (real-anchoring).

claims: Culture is misconceived as a finished, transmissible object and rightly conceived as a generation that does not close.

Culture is the dialectical exteriorization across the three registers, under material constraint, of the interwoven generative history of relational subjects — with the Real granted a relational form.

The intimate dyad is the minimal and most exposed unit of cultural emergence, with five mechanisms proper to it (vacant big Other, interweaving of drive, high-density sedimentation, register configuration, fragility).
Capital, having exhausted older frontiers, reaches into the bond itself and captures the value it generates by decoherence — preserving the symbolic form while draining its coherence in the Real.
The just generation of culture depends on the generation of value, which carries power, also generating in the same movement the counter-power that restrains power and prevents its entrenchment.
A relational culture's resistance to transfer, and to power, capital, and time, rises with the depth of its anchoring in interwoven drive and in the register of the Real.
papers/paper-24.pdf.conclusion: Culture, seen where it is smallest, turns out not to be an inheritance but an act — an unfinished generation that two people carry out together across the imaginary, the symbolic, and the real, under the weight of their material conditions. Granting the Real a relational form lets the paper name what larger accounts of culture miss: the vacant authority the dyad must supply for itself, the interweaving of two desires, the fast sedimentation and the fragility of a world only two people hold. That same fragility is what capital exploits — capturing an intimate culture by decoherence, keeping its symbolic shell while draining its life in the Real — and the paper's ethics answers in kind: a culture is justly and durably generated only when the value it makes, which always carries power, generates in the same movement the counter-power that keeps power from entrenching. The argument closes with a cross-scale retrospect and an envoi, having shown the two-person bond to be the exemplary and most revealing site of culture as such.
contributions: A relational reconception of culture as a generation that does not close, developed across an ontology, a phenomenology, and an ethics.
The three-register dialectic of the relational Real — a variant of Lacan's three registers that grants the Real a relational form and sets the registers in materially driven dialectical motion.
Five mechanisms proper to the intimate dyad as the minimal unit of cultural emergence, with the family ethos (jiafeng) as a middle-scale case.
A political economy of intimate culture, including capture-as-decoherence — how capital drains a bond's coherence in the Real while preserving its symbolic form.
The counter-power criterion for the just and durable generation of culture.
Five original theses (non-transferability, vacancy, capture-as-decoherence, counter-power criterion, real-anchoring) beyond the revision of Lacan.

outline.gist: How culture emerges in general: passes through transmission, symbol, reproduction, power, the wen–hua tradition, and the dialogic to reach the three-register dialectic of the relational Real; culture as the exteriorization of drive, the dialectic of the material and ideal, a definition of cultural emergence in intimate relation, and the sublation of power and of cultural evolution.

Cultural phenomena in the intimate dyad: intimate relation as a special site; participatory knowing and epistemic exclusivity; and the five pillars — the dyad and the vacant big Other, the double interweaving of drive, high-density sedimentation and accelerated time, the special configuration of the three registers, and fragility and reversibility — with the hermeneutics of private culture and its negotiation with the outer symbolic order.

Production, capture, and lessons: family ethos (jiafeng) as a middle-scale case; the production of culture; the capture of intimate culture by capital; the closed loop back into the bond; constrained but not determined; the ethics of cultural cognition and practice; and a cross-scale retrospect and envoi.
